meta.description: Daily tick; per active search_engagement, decides via the hub whether a rank pull is DUE (tool_scope.rank.cadence vs. the property's own last rank-snapshot capture time — never a hardcoded schedule, never n8n's own memory) and, if so, fires the real search.pullRanks MCP tool (SM-14; posts a DataForSEO Standard-queue task through the full scope/budget/pillar choke-point). Mode-blind by construction: nothing here reads providerMode or config.search.* — the platform's dispatch path is the sole mode authority (tracker seo-sem-execution-tracker.md #6j). Scoped identity wf:sm-rank-pull -> [search.listEngagements, search.rankSummary, search.pullRanks, approvals.request]. Env: HUB_SERVICE_TOKEN, AGENCY_TENANT_ID (both already used by other flows in this compose). ⚠️ CONFIRMED LIVE-BLOCKED as of 2026-07-30 (see the ticket report): modules/search/index.ts declares search.pullRanks minAssurance:'verified', but every automation (n8n OBO) principal is minted assurance:'low' by construction (mcp-hub/src/principal.ts -- 'verified principals will come from the platform IdP... never from an envelope'). The hub's assurance check runs BEFORE the allow-list/impact-gate checks, so this call is denied for EVERY workflow, regardless of allow-list scope or approvals wiring -- proven live: 'denied: search.pullRanks requires verified assurance; caller has low'. Every other automation-reachable write tool in this hub (projects.create, tasks.create, tasks.update, notify, pipeline.*) is minAssurance:'low' -- this looks like an authoring oversight on the search.* mcpTools entries, not a deliberate decision (index.ts's own comment says paid pulls are impact:'medium' specifically so they route through the D14 AUTOMATION write gate, which presupposes automation can reach them at all). DO NOT activate this workflow until platform-nest lowers search.pullRanks's minAssurance to 'low' (a one-line index.ts change, outside this ticket's file ownership). Once that lands, this workflow's suspend-handling below (added because impact:'medium' will still route every run through a human-approval suspension, by design, per WS4 D14) is the part that then needs its own first live run to confirm.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ jsonrpc: "2.0", id: 1, method: "tools/call", params: { name: "search.pullRanks", arguments: { tenantId: $json.tenantId, engagementId: $json.engagementId } } }) }}

={{ JSON.stringify({ jsonrpc: "2.0", id: 1, method: "tools/call", params: { name: "approvals.request", arguments: { tenantId: $json.tenantId, workflowId: "wf:sm-rank-pull", toolName: $json.toolName, toolArgs: $json.toolArgs, impact: $json.impact, reason: $json.reason } } }) }}
